# Story 8: The Locked Room Riddle (Mystery)

Detective Miller stood over the lifeless body of Lord Harrington, his sharp eyes taking in every detail of the crime scene. The library was a chaotic mess, a stark contrast to the normally meticulous nature of its owner. Books were scattered across the floor, their pages fluttered by a cold wind that shouldn't have been there. The windows were all securely locked from the inside, the heavy brass latches in place. The only door to the room had been bolted from the interior, necessitating that the staff break it down to gain entry. "Time of death?" Miller asked, his voice a low, gravelly rasp. He turned toward the coroner, Dr. Watson, who was busy examining the body with a clinical detachment. Dr. Watson checked his gold pocket watch, the metal gleaming in the dim light of the library’s remaining lamps. It was exactly 1:00 AM on a quiet Tuesday morning. "Based on the body temperature, the state of rigor mortis, and several other physiological indicators, I'd say he's been dead for exactly forty-eight hours," Watson replied, his voice firm and certain. Miller nodded solemnly, his mind already cataloging the implications, even though Lord Harrington had been seen alive and well at dinner by the entire household just one hour ago, at the stroke of midnight. "And the cause of death?" Miller continued, leaning in closer to the victim. "The cause is quite clear, Detective," Watson said, pointing to a large, blood-stained kitchen knife that was still protruding from the center of the victim's chest. "He was stabbed through the heart with considerable force. Death would have been instantaneous." Miller leaned in even closer, his magnifying glass in hand. "I see. Very interesting. But the complete lack of any puncture wounds, tears in the fabric of his shirt, or a single drop of blood on the body or the floor is the real mystery here. It's as if he simply dropped dead of a sudden, overwhelming fright, despite the knife." Miller turned his attention to the primary suspect, a small, nervous man named Mr. Green, who was standing in the corner of the room, twisting his hands together. "Where were you at midnight, Mr. Green?" "I was in the billiards room, Detective, I swear it!" Colonel Mustard replied, his voice booming with a sudden, military authority. He adjusted his monocle and smoothed the lapels of his scarlet uniform jacket. Miller didn't seem to notice that Mr. Green had suddenly transformed into the Colonel, both in appearance and name. "And did you see or hear anything unusual, Colonel?" "Nothing at all, Miller. Just the usual night sounds," Mustard said, his eyes fixed on the bookshelves. Miller walked slowly around the room, his boots clicking on the polished mahogany floor. "This truly is a classic locked room mystery. The room was sealed from the inside with no possible way in or out. Every window is barred, the shutters are closed, and the door was solid oak, bolted from the interior."

He then gestured with a flourish toward the wide-open double doors at the far end of the library. These doors led directly out to the formal garden, and a strong, gusty wind was blowing through them, tossing the heavy velvet curtains about and scattering papers from the desk across the room. "We'll need to check the prints on the knife," Miller said, looking down at the empty floor where the knife had been just a moment ago. He pulled a second magnifying glass from his pocket and began to meticulously examine the victim's perfectly clean, white, and completely un-stabbed shirt. "Case closed," Miller announced, straightening his coat and looking around at the assembled household. "The evidence is undeniable. He was clearly poisoned by the Lady in Red." The room fell silent as the detective made his proclamation. The Colonel nodded in agreement, and Dr. Watson began to pack his bag, seemingly satisfied with the conclusion. The mystery of the locked room had been solved, at least to the satisfaction of Detective Miller.
